If you're using a controller these (www.amazon.com/KontrolFreek-Ultra-Xbox-One/dp/B00HUWANOO/) help out a lot with minute analog control.

They're not essential and not a substitute for mouse+keyboard, but they're nice if you like to use gamepads.

That's a good tip :) my brother uses something like these for Xbox One because he does a lot of sniping and benefits from the increased precision at the potential cost of quick movement.

Personally I enjoy using keyboard and mouse for a lot of PC games, but there's something about a controller that's just comfortable. And analog movement is important to a lot of games.

I use Xpadder on a lot of games, too. You can do some neat stuff with it. In the past few years developers have been a lot better with controller support and customization, tho.

It's great for those games where movement is better with analog (or even the d-pad), but all the hot keys on the keyboard are invaluable. In about 5 minutes you can create a custom mapping, and you can switch back and forth between gamepad and keyboard/mouse if one part of the game, like the menu, works better with a mouse.
